facts.statement: The genus Cyamodus was described by Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer in 1863 based on fossils found in Germany.
facts.quote: The genus was described by Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer in 1863, based on specimens found in Germany.

facts.statement: Cyamodus possessed an armored carapace made of irregular hexagonal plates and large rounded teeth adapted for crushing hard-shelled prey.
facts.quote: Like some other placodonts, Cyamodus has an armoured carapace composed of irregular hexagonal plates, with the mouth containing a small number of large, rounded teeth that were likely involved in crushing hard shelled organisms (durophagy).

facts.statement: Six species of Cyamodus have been identified: C. rostratus, C. munsteri, C. tarnowitzensis, C. hildegardis, C. kuhnschneyderi, and C. orientalis.
facts.quote: Thus far, six species of Cyamodus have been identified - C. rostratus, C. munsteri, C. tarnowitzensis, C. hildegardis, C. kuhnschneyderi, and C. orientalis.

facts.statement: The first Cyamodus remains were discovered in Upper Muschelkalk shallow marine limestones near Bayreuth in Bavaria, Germany.
facts.quote: Historically, the first Cyamodus remains were found in Upper Muschelkalk shallow marine limestones at near Bayreuth in Bavaria (Germany).

facts.statement: A complete skeleton of C. hildegardis was found in Switzerland outside the Germanic Basin in the northern Tethys.
facts.quote: A complete Cyamodus skeleton, including its skull, is known for C. hildegardis, which was found outside the Germanic Basin in the northern Tethys in Switzerland.

facts.statement: Most Cyamodus species were 1.3 to 1.5 meters long and weighed 20 to 25 kilograms, while the smallest species, C. rostratus, was about 0.9 meters long and weighed 5 kilograms.
facts.quote: Cyamodus was a relatively small reptile, with most species measuring 1.3 - 1.5 m long and weighing 20 - 25 kg; the smallest species, C. rostratus, was about 0.9 m long and weighed 5 kg.

facts.statement: Cyamodus was a heavily armored swimmer specialized in uprooting and crushing shellfish with its powerful jaws.
facts.quote: It was a heavily armored swimmer that fed mainly on shellfish that it was specialized to uproot and crush with its powerful jaws.

facts.statement: Cyamodus had a turtle-like flat body with a two-part carapace on its upper surface.
facts.quote: The body of Cyamodus, specifically the armor, has been described as possessing a turtle-like flatness. The shell was a two-part carapace on the upper surface of the body.

facts.statement: The skull of Cyamodus was heart-shaped and broad.
facts.quote: The skull is heart-shaped and broad.

facts.statement: Cyamodus lacked dorsal spines but possessed a wing-like, elongated, flattened lateral spine that braced the subdermal carapace.
facts.quote: Cyamodus did not have any dorsal spines, although it did have a wing-like elongated flattened lateral spine that served to brace the overlying subdermal carapace.

facts.statement: Cyamodus was more agile than other single-shelled placodonts like Henodus, despite its cumbersome shell.
facts.quote: Although the shell would most likely have been too cumbersome for highly adept swimming, Cyamodus would still have been more agile than other single shelled placodonts like Henodus.

facts.statement: The hexagonal plates on Cyamodus's shell increased protection and weight, an adaptation that helped it dive to reach shellfish.
facts.quote: The shells were also covered in hexagonal plates that not only increased the level of protection but also increased their weight, a typical placodont adaptation as additional weight just beyond the level of neutral buoyancy allowed them to dive to reach shellfish.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence of two Cyamodus juveniles inside a Lariosaurus stomach suggests the species was vulnerable to predation.
facts.quote: Discovery of two fossil Cyamodus juveniles inside the stomach area of a Lariosaurus fossil has led to speculation about its vulnerability to predation.

facts.statement: While C.G. Diedrich suggested Cyamodus was an algae-grazer, this view is widely rejected by researchers like Torsten M. Scheyer, and the consensus remains that placodonts (except Henodus) were durophagous.
facts.quote: C.G. Diedrich has suggested that Cyamodus and other placodonts were algae-grazers. However, this interpretation has been criticized by Torsten M. Scheyer and other researchers, and many subsequent studies about placodonts have rejected Deidrich's interpretation, and the consensus that placodonts with the exception of Henodus were durophagous still continues to be strongly supported.

facts.statement: Cyamodus was initially thought to be an ancestral turtle but was later reclassified as a placodont related to other Triassic turtle-like reptiles.
facts.quote: Initially considered to be an ancestral turtle due to its testudine-like head and large, bifurcated carapace. However further investigation resulted in its reclassification as a placodont, and it is closely related to other turtle-like reptiles of the Triassic period such as Henodus and Psephoderma.

facts.statement: Cyamodus belongs to the order Placodontia, suborder Sauropterygia, superfamily Cyamodontoidea, and family Cyamodontidae.
facts.quote: superordo: Sauropterygia ordo: Placodontia superfamilia: Cyamodontoidea familia: Cyamodontidae genus: Cyamodus genus_authority: Meyer, 1863

facts.statement: The genus Cyamodus was named by Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer in 1863.
facts.quote: Cyamodus es un género extinto de saurópsidos placodontes pertenecientes a la familia Cyamodontidae, los cuales fueron descubiertos en lo que hoy es Alemania entre inicios y mediados del y fue nombrado por Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer en 1863

facts.statement: Fossils of Cyamodus date from the Middle Triassic, specifically from the Anisian to Ladinian stages.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles se han datado de mediados del período Triásico, de las épocas del Anisiense al Ladiniense.

facts.statement: Cyamodus likely lived by foraging on the sea floor, sucking up shellfish, and crushing them with its blunt teeth.
facts.quote: De forma similar a estos otros placodontos, Cyamodus viviría de cernir el fondo de los mares, aspirando mariscos, y triturándolos con sus dientes romos.

facts.statement: The first remains of Cyamodus were found in shallow sea limestones of the Upper Muschelkalk near Bayreuth in Bavaria, Germany.
facts.quote: Históricamente, los primeros restos de Cyamodus fueron encontrados en las calizas de mares someros del Muschelkalk Superior cerca de Bayreuth en Baviera (Alemania).

facts.statement: The only known complete skeleton of Cyamodus, including the skull, is that of C. hildegardis, found outside the German Basin in the northern Tethys Sea in present-day Switzerland.
facts.quote: El único esqueleto completo conocido de Cyamodus, incluyendo el cráneo, es el de C. hildegardis, el cual fue encontrado por fuera de la Cuenca germánica en el norte del mar de Tetis en la actual Suiza.

facts.statement: Cyamodus was a heavily armored swimmer measuring 1.3 meters in length that specialized in digging up and crushing shellfish with its powerful jaws.
facts.quote: Cyamodus era un nadador pesadamente acorazado, de 1.3 metros de longitud, el cual se alimentaba de mariscos en los que se especializaba en desenterrar y triturar con sus poderosas mandíbulas.

facts.statement: The body of Cyamodus, specifically its armor, is described as similar to that of turtles due to its flattened shape.
facts.quote: El cuerpo de Cyamodus, y específicamente su armadura, se ha descrito como similar al de las tortugas por su forma aplanada.

facts.statement: The skull of Cyamodus was wide and heart-shaped.
facts.quote: El cráneo era ancho y en forma de corazón.

facts.statement: The teeth resembled flat discs, with only one tooth in each premaxilla and two in each maxilla, while the largest teeth were located in the pterygoid.
facts.quote: Los dientes semejaban discos planos, con solo un diente en cada premaxilar y solo dos dientes en cada maxilar, mientras que los dientes de mayor tamaño se situaban en el pterigoides.

facts.statement: Once considered a possible ancestor of turtles due to its wide, flattened torso covered in dermal osteoderms, it is now considered a very distant relative.
facts.quote: Considerado como un posible ancestro de las tortugas debido a su torso ancho y aplanado cubierto con osterdermos dérmicos, se lo considera ahora como un pariente muy distante.

facts.statement: Later research determined that it was reclassified as a placodont and closely related to other Triassic turtle-like reptiles such as Henodus and Psephoderma.
facts.quote: Posteriores investigaciones determinaron que fuera reclasificado como un placodonto, y cercanamente relacionado con otros reptiles similares a tortugas del período Triásico tales como Henodus y Psephoderma.

facts.statement: Cyamodus belongs to the parent group Cyamodontidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Cyamodontidae

facts.statement: Cyamodus is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Cyamodus is Cyamodus muensteri.
facts.quote: Type species: Cyamodus muensteri

facts.statement: An intriguing placodont described by Giovanni Pinna in 1990, Protenodontosaurus italicus, appears to be intermediate between Cyamodus and the placocheilids.
facts.quote: Un intrigante placodonto que parece ser intermedio entre Cyamodus y los placoquélidos, Protenodontosaurus italicus, fue descrito por Giovanni Pinna en 1990.
